title.narrative: Addressing the most urgent shelter needs of vulnerable people affected by Hurricane Beryl in Jamaica

description.narrative: The record-breaking early Category 4 storm Hurricane Beryl, caused widespread damage across multiple parishes in Jamaica, with varying levels of impact, Clarendon and St. Elizabeth parishes were greatly affected. Through this CERF Rapid Response allocation, IOM aims to immediately kick-start critical improvements to the emergency shelters and structures benefiting 13,500 individuals in the Clarendon and St. Elizabeth parishes. The interventions undertaken through this allocation will include 1) Emergency shelter repair/upgrade and 2) Provision of vouchers for purchase of shelter repair materials, and labour support for vulnerable households, including capacity building, to conduct repairs. Beneficiaries will receive USD 160 vouchers on average, depending on the identified needs. The demand for materials in Jamaica may be high, but local and national suppliers have been identified to address the materials demand from this intervention The project will mainstream protection, including gender equality, strong community engagement, the inclusion of and participation of vulnerable groups, protection/GBV risk mitigation. Planned interventions will integrate IOM’s accountability for affected population (AAP) and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) through engagement with specialists/focal points.
